I'm a 3D interactive avatar living inside a WebGL canvas.
Built with React Three Fiber and Three.js, I can move, react, and chat in real time!

What can you do?.reply:
I can walk, run, sit, and interact with objects in this 3D scene.
You can also trigger different animations by clicking the buttons in the experience.

How were you built?.reply:
I was built using React Three Fiber (R3F) on top of Three.js.
My animations come from a GLTF model, and physics are handled by Rapier via @react-three/rapier.

That's cool! What animations do you have.reply:
I have idle, walk, run, sit, and talk animations.
Each one blends smoothly using Three.js AnimationMixer under the hood.

What is React Three Fiber?.reply:
React Three Fiber is a React renderer for Three.js.
It lets you build 3D scenes using JSX components instead of raw Three.js imperative code.

How do I trigger animations?.reply:
Click the floating buttons in the 3D scene — like 'Sit and Talk' or 'Free Style'.
Each button triggers a different animation state on my character controller.

What is Rapier?.reply:
Rapier is a fast physics engine written in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly.
@react-three/rapier wraps it for easy use in R3F scenes — handling collisions, gravity, and rigid bodies.
